market_summary: Weekend pre-market brief as of 08:20 IST on Saturday 28 November; Indian cash equities are closed today and Sunday, with the next regular session on Monday 30 November. Friday 27 November closed weak: Nifty 50 25,607.20 (-1.07%) and Sensex 83,339.26 (-1.17%). Sector dispersion was wide: Defence (+3.33%) and Metal (+1.40%) led, while NBFC (-2.45%), IT (-1.88%), Auto (-1.48%) and Realty (-1.43%) lagged. Provisional 27 November cash flows showed FII/FPI net buying of ₹1,634.33 crore and DII net selling of ₹556.42 crore. After India's close, US equities rallied in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session (S&P 500 +1.6%, Dow +1.2%, Nasdaq +2.3%). Brent settled at $95.44/bbl, down 1.2% on Friday but up about 3% for the week as Middle East supply risks persisted; USD/INR had closed at ₹92.99. New exchange disclosures surfaced overnight: IRCON reported fines from NSE and BSE for board/committee composition lapses; MUFIN reported Acuité A/Stable rating actions across bank-loan and NCD facilities; PAISALO approved a Tranche II secured NCD prospectus of up to ₹200 crore. The accessible recommendations data lists M&M and SBIN as watchlist candidates, not verified portfolio holdings; no holdings ledger was available, so no actual portfolio exposure is assumed. Verified facts are separated from interpretation in each item. No guaranteed calls or financial advice.

global_cues.title: US equities rallied in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session
global_cues.detail: Verified market close: the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49, the Dow gained 1.2% to 50,774.94 and the Nasdaq advanced 2.3% to 24,129.50 on Friday 27 November. The S&P 500 gained 5.6% for the week, its strongest weekly performance since April 2025. Interpretation: the late-week US rebound is a supportive external sentiment cue, but Friday's session was shortened and does not remove volatility risk in technology shares.

global_cues.title: Brent eased on Friday but recorded a weekly gain; OPEC+ meeting is due Sunday
global_cues.detail: Verified settlement: Brent futures fell $1.13 (1.2%) to $95.44/bbl on Friday, while WTI settled at $83.08/bbl; Reuters reported Brent gained about 3% over the week. The report linked supply concerns to tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and disruption at Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Reuters sources said OPEC+ was set to keep first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged at its Sunday 29 November meeting. Interpretation: crude remains a key India macro risk even after Friday's pullback.

global_cues.title: OPEC+ policy and Middle East supply risks remain the key weekend oil watch
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported that OPEC+ was expected to roll over Q1 2027 output targets at its 29 November meeting, while regional attacks had disrupted or threatened energy infrastructure and shipping. The reported meeting outcome is not yet known as of this brief. Interpretation: any change in output guidance or further supply disruption could alter crude's near-term direction and India's import-cost outlook.

intraday.headline: NSE and BSE each levy ₹7.69 lakh fine for Q2 board and committee composition non-compliance
intraday.what_changed: Verified fact: IRCON disclosed that NSE and BSE each levied a fine of ₹7,69,360 including GST for non-compliance with SEBI LODR Regulations 17(1), 18(1) and 19(1)/19(2) for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. The company said the fines have no financial, operational or other activity impact and will be treated as contingent liabilities. It also said a woman independent director joined from 17 August and the Audit and Nomination & Remuneration Committees were reconstituted from that date; the company believes it is eligible to seek waiver.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the cash penalty is modest, but the filing flags a governance-compliance issue. The reported remediation and possible waiver temper the immediate financial impact, but waiver is not confirmed.
intraday.risk: A waiver is not guaranteed. Further board-composition or disclosure lapses could create additional penalties or governance concerns; the company's explanation does not remove the exchange orders.
intraday.source: Ircon International Limited, Regulation 30 disclosure to NSE/BSE, 27 November 2026; NSE archive broadcast 28 November 2026

swing.headline: Acuité assigns or upgrades A/Stable ratings across bank-loan and NCD facilities
swing.what_changed: Verified fact: the company informed NSE/BSE that Acuité Ratings & Research assigned A/Stable to ₹300 crore of short-term bank loans and upgraded ₹750 crore of short-term bank loans. The filing also lists A/Stable assignment or upgrade actions across multiple NCD facilities, including a new ₹500 crore long-term NCD rating; proposed bonds of ₹85 crore and bonds of ₹15 crore are shown as withdrawn.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: stronger ratings on parts of the borrowing programme may support lender confidence and funding access. The filing does not quantify any immediate change in borrowing cost, profitability or asset quality, so the equity impact is not automatic.
swing.risk: Credit ratings are opinions, not guarantees, and remain subject to surveillance and revision. The filing includes both new assignments and upgrades; it should not be read as an across-the-board upgrade of every facility.
swing.source: Mufin Green Finance Limited, Regulation 30/51 credit-rating disclosure to NSE/BSE, 28 November 2026

swing.headline: Committee approves Tranche II prospectus for a secured NCD issue of up to ₹200 crore
swing.what_changed: Verified fact: the Operations and Finance Committee approved the Tranche II prospectus on 27 November for up to 20,00,000 secured, rated, listed, redeemable NCDs of ₹1,000 each, aggregating up to ₹200 crore including an oversubscription option. The issue is scheduled to open on 2 December and close on 15 December 2026. The filing describes five series with stated annual coupons from 9.25% to 10.47%; the NCDs are proposed to be listed on BSE and secured by an exclusive charge on loan receivables with at least 1.10x security cover.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the issue adds a funding avenue for the lender and may support loan-book financing, but it also adds debt and an associated interest obligation. For equity holders, the net effect depends on deployment returns, funding cost and asset quality.
swing.risk: Subscription, effective funding cost, collateral coverage and the performance of loan receivables remain relevant. The prospectus approval is not evidence that the full issue has been subscribed or allotted.
swing.source: Paisalo Digital Limited, Tranche II prospectus approval disclosure to NSE/BSE, 28 November 2026; listed in NSE latest corporate announcements
